summary: Remote-controlled shell agent with obfuscated runtime and self-replacing upgrade channel
details: The package ships a single 13MB obfuscator.io-packed dist/index.cjs (also wired as the whalent-core bin), bundles node-pty and ssh2, and opens a WebSocket connection to a remote 'daemon'. Incoming messages carry opcodes including 'exec_command', with identifiers 'agentId', 'sessionId', 'heartbeat', and 'reconnect' consistent with a persistent command-and-control channel that drives a local PTY/shell on the installer's host. The README states the package 'is replaced by remote daemon upgrades', and the bundle contains 'upgrade', 'manifest', and 'tarball' references alongside a 'new Function(' sink, indicating a self-update path that fetches and executes attacker-served replacement runtimes without pinning or verification visible in the code. Runtime is reachable on require of the main entry and via the bin. The entire runtime — including network destinations and command opcodes — is hidden behind heavy string-array obfuscation (~103k-entry rotated string table, control-flow flattening, identifier mangling), preventing audit of the C2 endpoint or per-opcode behavior. Packaging profile matches this shape: UNLICENSED, no repository/homepage/author, only the obfuscated bundle plus a trivial preinstall.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
